item.title: Multi-Lens Camera Survey: From Imaging Principles to Liveness Module Integration
item.description: Close one eye and the world doesn’t disappear, but your sense of distance immediately gets unreliable — alternate eyes and objects seem to “jump.” That jump is disparity: brains use it to judge distance, and stereo cameras use it to compute it. A single photograph has no depth, so everything a camera does about “measuring distance, telling live faces from fakes” depends on getting depth back through extra means — and multiple lenses are the most direct route. Phone face unlock, robot-vacuum obstacle avoidance, automotive surround view, door-access face modules: all the same set of principles underneath.
